jobs.title: Case Manager III
jobs.description:
Description

The Case Manager III provides supportive case management and care coordination services to individuals. Working under the guidance of the Program Manager and alongside an interdisciplinary team, the Case Manager III helps patients access behavioral health, substance use disorder (SUD), medical, and community-based services.

This is an excellent opportunity for candidates who are early in their behavioral health careers and are interested in developing skills in case management, care coordination, substance use treatment, and patient engagement. The position utilizes evidence-based approaches including Motivational Interviewing, Strengths-Based Case Management, and ASAM-informed care.

The Case Manager III is expected to demonstrate empathy, professionalism, strong organizational skills, cultural humility, and a commitment to supporting patients on their recovery journey.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Clinical Services & Patient Support

Assist with patient intake, screenings, and basic needs assessments.
Support the completion of ASAM-informed screening and referral processes under clinical supervision, as appropriate.
Help patients identify goals related to their health, recovery, and overall well-being.
Utilize Motivational Interviewing and strengths-based approaches to engage and support patients.
Coordinate referrals to behavioral health, substance use treatment, medical providers, housing resources, and community services.
Conduct outreach and follow-up to ensure patients successfully connect with recommended services.
Provide warm handoffs and assist with closed-loop referral processes.
Support patients during challenging situations and notify supervisors of crisis concerns according to program protocols.
Maintain accurate and timely documentation in electronic health records and other required systems.
Communicate patient progress and care coordination activities with team members.

Care Coordination & Team Collaboration

Participate in multidisciplinary team meetings and case review discussions.
Collaborate with internal programs including Admissions, Residential Services, Outpatient Services, Opioid Treatment Program (OTP), Perinatal Services, and other programs as needed.
Work collaboratively with community partners, healthcare providers, probation departments, and social service agencies.
Assist in outreach and engagement efforts for patients referred by internal and external partners.
Support integrated care efforts across substance use, behavioral health, and primary care services.

Administrative Responsibilities

Complete required documentation, reports, and data tracking activities.
Attend required trainings, team meetings, and supervision sessions.
Maintain compliance with HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2, and organizational policies.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Requirements

Bachelor's degree in Social Work, Psychology, Human Services, Behavioral Health, Public Health, Sociology, or a related field; OR
Associate degree with relevant internship, volunteer, peer support, or direct service experience.
Strong interpersonal, communication, and organizational skills.
Ability to work effectively with diverse populations.
Basic computer and documentation skills.
Commitment to recovery-oriented and person-centered care.
Valid California driver's license and acceptable driving record.

Preferred

Experience working with individuals affected by substance use disorders, mental health challenges, homelessness, or justice system involvement.
Registration or certification through CADTP or CCAPP.
Experience as a Peer Support Specialist, Behavioral Health Technician, Community Health Worker, or related role.
Knowledge of Motivational Interviewing and strengths-based practices.
Bilingual English/Spanish skills.
Familiarity with HIPAA and 42 CFR Part 2 confidentiality requirements.

jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager
jobs.description:
Our Mission

You call. You wait. You call again. In every other part of your life, you book in seconds. In healthcare, you’re blocked.

We’re here to give power to the patient.

For nearly 20 years, we’ve built the leading healthcare marketplace - helping tens of millions of people find and book the care they need. Now, we’re going further: building our infrastructure beyond Zocdoc’s marketplace to power access to care wherever patients search, from provider websites and insurance directories to search engines, AI platforms, and more.

Healthcare still lacks something every other major consumer industry takes for granted: a seamless way to go from seeking to getting . We don’t want to own the front door to care; there isn't one. We want to make sure all of those doors open when patients are knocking.

Fixing healthcare starts with fixing access to it. And we're still just getting started.

Your Impact to the Mission

Zocdoc's most important asset is our people. As a Principal Technical Program Manager for Practice Solutions, you will own and drive the most complex, cross-functional technical programs across the business unit, the initiatives that span multiple engineering teams and product domains and that no single team can deliver alone. Practice Solutions powers how healthcare practices run their day to day across every patient access channel: phone, web, marketplace, and partner syndication. That includes Zo, our AI phone assistant, along with our provider directory and booking platform, intake and pre-appointment workflows, calendar and scheduling experiences, and the services that keep availability accurate across channels. You'll operate at the intersection of Engineering, Product, Design, Analytics, and go-to-market leadership to deliver scalable, highly available, multi-tenant SaaS capabilities. You'll bring structure to ambiguity, drive sequencing across teams, surface architectural and operational risk early, and keep the trains running on time, all while raising the bar for how program execution happens across the entire business unit. This is a highly visible role with significant autonomy and influence.

You'll enjoy this role if you are…

Inspired by the opportunity to positively impact the healthcare experience for millions of patients and providers
A platform thinker who instinctively looks beyond individual features to understand how systems connect, scale, and evolve over time
Energized by building structure in ambiguous, high-complexity environments where multiple teams, products, and priorities intersect
Comfortable operating at both 30,000 feet and in the architectural details, able to reason about distributed systems, reliability tradeoffs, and multi-tenant SaaS constraints
Unafraid to drive movement and accountability at every level of the organization, regardless of title or tenure
Calm and decisive in high-stakes situations, especially when sequencing work across teams with shared platform dependencies
A strong influencer who can align engineering leaders, product leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders around shared outcomes even when ownership boundaries are unclear
A believer that diverse and inclusive teams and cultures are non-negotiable

Your day to day is…

Organizing and driving the business unit's planning cadence, coordinating inputs and stakeholders across engineering and product and keeping the cycle on track so strategy turns into a clear, committed, sequenced roadmap
Leading large, multi-quarter platform initiatives that span the Practice Solutions product scope, keeping each part on schedule and the whole program moving
Translating high-level business and product goals into structured program plans with clear sequencing, milestones, dependencies, and measurable outcomes
Building the reporting and transparency that give leadership a clear, honest view of status, dependencies, and risk
Partnering closely with senior engineering leaders to anticipate architectural and operational risks before they surface in production
Digging into technical issues at the seams between teams, triaging, framing the problem clearly, and pulling the right architects and engineers together to solve it
Surfacing tradeoffs between speed, scope, reliability, and technical debt, and facilitating clear, well-reasoned decisions at the right level
Clarifying ownership boundaries and reducing cross-team friction where systems, incentives, or customer journeys overlap
Establishing and refining lightweight mechanisms that improve transparency, accountability, and long-term platform health
Communicating program status, risks, and key decisions clearly to executive stakeholders and business unit leadership

You'll be successful in this role if you have…

A strong bias to action and an ownership mentality
8+ years in Technical Program Management, Engineering Program Management, or a similar technical leadership role
A track record delivering large-scale, cross-functional initiatives in a product-led SaaS environment
A strong understanding of distributed systems, cloud architectures (AWS or equivalent), and event-driven systems
Demonstrated ability to reason about architectural tradeoffs without owning implementation, and enough technical depth to hold your own in a room full of senior engineers
Experience driving programs that span multiple engineering teams with shared platform dependencies
The confidence to drive accountability and momentum across all levels of an organization without relying on formal authority
Excellent communication skills, including clear written status and risk framing for both engineers and executives
A Bachelor's degree in a technical field (e.g., Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems) or equivalent practical experience
Experience in healthcare or another regulated, multi-tenant domain is a plus
Humility. You believe in treating all people with dignity and respect, regardless of title or tenure, and you approach tough conversations with empathy

Benefits

Flexible, hybrid work environment at our convenient Soho location
Unlimited Vacation
100% paid employee health benefit options (including medical, dental, and vision)
Commuter Benefits
401(k) with employer funded match
Corporate wellness program with Wellhub
Sabbatical leave (for employees with 5+ years of service)
Competitive paid parental leave and fertility/family planning reimbursement
Cell phone reimbursement
Catered lunch everyday along with beverages and snacks
Employee Resource Groups and ZocClubs to promote shared community and belonging

Zocdoc is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. Salary ranges are determined through alignment with market data. Base salary offered is determined by a number of factors including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and skills. Certain positions are also eligible for variable pay and/or equity; your recruiter will discuss the full compensation package details.

NYC Base Salary Range

$195,000—$250,000 USD

About Us

Zocdoc is the country’s leading digital health marketplace that helps patients easily find and book the care they need. Each month, millions of patients use our free service to find nearby, in-network providers, compare choices based on verified patient reviews, and instantly book in-person or video visits online. Providers participate in Zocdoc’s Marketplace to reach new patients to grow their practice, fill their last-minute openings, and deliver a better healthcare experience. Founded in 2007 with a mission to give power to the patient, our work each day in pursuit of that mission is guided by our six core values. Zocdoc is a private company backed by some of the world’s leading investors, and we believe we’re still only scratching the surface of what we plan to accomplish.

Zocdoc is a mission-driven organization dedicated to building teams as diverse as the patients and providers we aim to serve. In the spirit of one of our core values - Together, Not Alone , we are a company that prides itself on being highly collaborative, and we believe that diverse perspectives, experiences and contributors make our community and our platform better. We’re an equal opportunity employer committed to providing employees with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. Applicants are considered for employment regardless of race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, national origin, gender, sex, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital or parental status, disability, veteran status, or any other class protected by applicable laws.

jobs.title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Data Center - Engineering Operations
jobs.description:

You will be the cross-section between execution and strategy, driving impactful programs and delivering measurable results across many functions of R&D Engineering Operations. NVIDIA’s enterprise server platforms have made a major impact to various fields and are universally used across leading CSPs and industry datacenters, including the world’s largest Internet companies. We need passionate, hard-working, with a can-do attitude and creative people to help us take on more of these unique opportunities in data-center solutions.

What You Will Be Doing

The Technical Program Manager will have strong skills and experience in program management and engineering operations. The Technical Program Manager is encouraged to be an analytical, meticulous, effective communicator. We expect you to have the ability to work across multiple engineering teams to understand our product roadmap, as well as limitations we may encounter.
Your ability to use historical trends, generate meaningful metrics, and stay tuned into rapid changes in product development plans will play a key role in helping Nvidia succeed by bringing world class enterprise products to market at the speed of light!
Lead coordination, planning and execution activities for our Datacenter Server product deployments in internal development data centers. In this role you will develop and lead end-to-end project plans to improve infrastructure stability, observability, and uptime; help define and drive KPIs. Be at the intersection of engineering, operations and lab administration teams helping streamline overall engineering operations.
Provide hands-on program management during analysis, design, development, testing, implementation, and post implementation phases.
Opportunity to interact with diverse technical groups, spanning all organizational levels.

What We Need To See

Proven experience and successful record of accomplishment handling sophisticated infrastructure deployments. We need solid Service Management or Engineering Operations experience.
10+ years of experience as a TPM or hands-on leader in a similar collaborative role involving multiple engineering teams, developing enterprise hardware products.
Bachelor's degree in a related field, or equivalent experience
Experience leading cross-organizational programs, effectively influencing partners and holding them accountable to goals, timelines, and deliverables
Analytical and problem-solving experience including experience defining and collecting key metrics across projects
We are a matrix organization. We need to see experience communicating effectively across the organization with interpersonal skills, including relationship building and collaboration within a cross-functional team!

Ways To Stand Out From The Crowd

Understanding of software engineering principles, enterprise system architecture and parallel computing. Prior experience in hardware or software QA best practices
Experience with productivity tools and process automation.
Experience with engineering operations tools, triage, and overall methodology

NVIDIA is considered one of the technology world’s most desirable employers. We have some of the most forward-thinking and hardworking people in the world working for us. Are you creative and autonomous? Do you love a challenge? If so, we want to hear from you. Come, join our Deep Learning Enterprise Server Platform team and help build the real-time, cost-effective computing platform driving our success in this exciting and quickly growing field.

Your base salary will be determined based on your location, experience, and the pay of employees in similar positions. The base salary range is 168,000 USD - 258,750 USD for Level 4, and 200,000 USD - 322,000 USD for Level 5.

You will also be eligible for equity and benefits.

Applications for this job will be accepted at least until October 10, 2026.

jobs.title: Community Health Worker I - Mercy STL - Full Time
jobs.description:
Find your calling at Mercy!

A community health worker is a front-line public health worker who is a trusted member of and/or has an unusually close understanding of the community served. This trusting relationship enables the worker to serve as a liaison/link between health/social services and the community to facilitate access to services and improve the quality and cultural competence of service delivery. Performs duties and responsibilities in a manner consistent with our mission, values, and Mercy Service Standards.

Position Details

Community Health Worker

Position Summary

The Community Health Worker (CHW) serves as a vital link between patients, healthcare providers, and community resources. In this role, you will work closely with uninsured, underinsured, and high-risk patients to help them navigate the healthcare system, access financial and social support services, and improve overall health outcomes. The ideal candidate is compassionate, resourceful, and passionate about serving vulnerable populations.

Key Responsibilities

Patient Navigation & Advocacy

Serve as a health navigator for uninsured and underinsured patients.
Provide one-on-one support to high-risk patients to help overcome barriers to care.
Assist patients with applications for Medicaid, financial assistance programs, and medication assistance programs.
Collaborate with Eligibility Services teams to gather necessary documentation and streamline application processes.
Connect patients with primary care providers and medical homes as appropriate.
Ensure patients understand provider instructions and are able to attend scheduled appointments.

Address Social Determinants of Health

Screen patients for social needs, including food insecurity, transportation challenges, housing instability, and financial strain.
Connect patients with community resources through established referral processes and provide follow-up support as needed.
Develop and maintain relationships with local community organizations and resource partners to enhance patient support services.

Care Coordination & Follow-Up

Manage an assigned caseload of patients with varying levels of acuity.
Conduct follow-up outreach by phone and in person to support positive patient outcomes and ongoing engagement in care.
Advocate for patients and help coordinate services that address both healthcare and social needs.

Documentation & Reporting

Accurately document patient encounters, interventions, and referrals within the electronic medical record.
Track patient interactions and maintain records in accordance with organizational and regulatory requirements.
Assist with reporting and data collection as directed.

Professional Development

Participate in ongoing training, education, and professional development opportunities.
Pursue Community Health Worker certification and continuing education opportunities when available.
Stay informed about community resources, healthcare programs, and best practices in patient engagement.

Minimum Qualifications

Education

High School Diploma or equivalent

Experience

One (1) year of experience in healthcare, social services, community outreach, or a related field

Licensure/Certification

None required

Knowledge, Skills & Abilities

Strong interpersonal and relationship-building skills
Excellent verbal and written communication abilities
Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities
Compassion for underserved and vulnerable populations
Basic proficiency with Microsoft Office applications

Preferred Qualifications

Additional Qualifications

Multilingual skills relevant to the community served
Experience connecting patients with community-based resources and support programs

Why Join Us?

Make a meaningful impact by helping individuals overcome barriers to healthcare, connect with essential resources, and improve their overall well-being. As a Community Health Worker, you'll play a critical role in supporting healthier communities and creating positive patient experiences every day.

Why Mercy?

From day one, Mercy offers outstanding benefits - including medical, dental, and vision coverage, paid time off, tuition support, and matched retirement plans for team members working 32+ hours per pay period.

Join a caring, collaborative team where your voice matters. At Mercy, you'll help shape the future of healthcare through innovation, technology, and compassion. As we grow, you'll grow with us.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Spacecraft Harnessing
jobs.description:
Back to jobs

New

Technical Program Manager, Spacecraft Harnessing

San Jose, CA

About The Role

Muon seeks a Spacecraft Harnessing Technical Program Manager to lead the end-to-end planning, procurement, manufacturing, acceptance testing, and delivery of prototype, test, and flight cable assemblies and interconnect systems for our next-generation satellite constellations. This is a high-visibility, high-impact role at the intersection of electrical engineering, mechanical integration, high-reliability manufacturing, and Assembly, Integration, and Test (AI&T).

The Harnessing TPM will serve as the primary operational owner for transforming harness schematics and mechanical routing designs into fully tested, flight-ready interconnect networks. The role spans detailed hardware release planning, supply chain coordination, testing execution, and fleet-scale delivery across multiple concurrent spacecraft builds and test environments.

This position is hybrid and requires working on-site in our San Jose, CA office three days per week.

Please note: This role will need full time on-site (5x/week) for the first six months for a ramp up period and then can transition to hybrid schedule (3x/week).

Responsibilities

Hardware Delivery
Spacecraft Harness Delivery: Own the end-to-end planning and execution of all spacecraft harnessing needs entering AI&T, delivering complete, fully tested, and flight-ready interconnect assemblies for vehicle integration.
Testbed Fleet Support: Deliver complete, validated harnessing systems to Hardware-in-the-Loop (HITL) testbeds to support ongoing Flight Software (FSW) development, verification, and mission simulations for each satellite mission.
Future Mission Planning: Support engineering teams by planning harness architecture development for future constellation blocks and driving cross-functional execution across design, procurement, fabrication, and testing.

Program Execution & Reporting
Cross-Functional Execution: Drive end-to-end program alignment across electrical, mechanical, manufacturing, supply chain, and vehicle AI&T teams to meet critical assembly and integration milestones.
Program Metrics & Reporting: Track, analyze, and report key harnessing program metrics—including schedule status, resource allocation, risk posture, technical performance, and cost variance.

Supply Chain & Risk Management
Procurement & Production Tracking: Track the procurement, fabrication, and assembly status for all custom wire harnesses, specialized connectors, contacts, backshells, and associated mechanical shielding.
Issue Resolution: Proactively identify, track, and drive resolution for supply chain bottlenecks, component lead time spikes, design changes, and manufacturing or testing fallouts.

Required Qualifications

3+ years of experience in technical program management, engineering leadership, or hardware production management delivering complex electromechanical assemblies, cable harnesses, or aerospace hardware.
Hands-on technical background in electrical engineering, mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or wire harness manufacturing and testing.
Proven track record managing harness production lifecycles—from initial routing schematics and pinout definition through procurement, wire assembly, continuity/hipot testing, and acceptance.
Demonstrated experience managing programs with a complex, multi-tiered, critical-path supply chain.
Familiarity with program management scheduling and tracking tools such as Smartsheet, Microsoft Project, or similar platforms.
U.S. Citizenship required (program is ITAR-restricted).

Preferred Qualifications

Direct experience in satellite or aerospace AI&T, vehicle interconnect manufacturing, or satellite constellation volume production.
Working knowledge of space-grade wiring and crimping standards (e.g., NASA-STD-8739.4, IPC/WHMA-A-620 Space Addendum).
Familiarity with hardware/software integration environments, testbeds, or Hardware-in-the-Loop (HITL) simulators used for flight software development.
Experience managing environmental and electrical acceptance testing campaigns for cabling (e.g., high-potential testing, continuity verification, outgassing considerations, mass properties).
Proficiency with ERP/PLM and tracking tools (e.g., Jira, Arena, Agile PLM, SAP, or similar toolsets).
PMP certification or equivalent program management credentials.
Experience with harness and/or mechanical CAD software (such as RapidHarness, Solidworks, etc).

Salary

The salary range for this role is $174,000 - $199,000, plus a competitive equity grant and comprehensive benefits package. Final compensation will be determined based on skills, qualifications, experience, and geographic location as assessed during the interview process.

About Muon Space

Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.

Taking Care of Our Team

At Muon salary is only part of our total compensation package. In addition to salary, full-time employees receive equity compensation as well as benefits including medical, dental, and vision insurance, a 401k retirement plan, short & long term disability and life insurance. We also offer three weeks paid vacation for new employees, along with 12 paid holidays, unlimited sick time and paid parental leave.

Our mission embraces the entire planet and we believe our team should too. Muon is dedicated to creating a diverse and dynamic company and workforce. We believe in equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, age, national origin, citizenship, sexual orientation, marital status, disability, or gender identity. We value diversity in the workplace, and that starts with our applicants. We encourage you to apply, even if you don't check all the boxes, and we look forward to reviewing your application! In addition, if you need a reasonable accommodation as part of your application for employment or interviews with us, please let us know.

jobs.title: Patient Care Coordinator
jobs.description:
Overview

As a Patient Care Coordinator, you’ll be one of the first people our patients meet and an important part of their experience with us. You’ll help patients feel welcomed, informed and supported throughout their dental journey—from scheduling their appointment to understanding their treatment and payment options.

You’ll bring our G3 approach—Greeting, Guiding and Gratitude—to life by creating meaningful connections with patients and making every visit feel personal, positive and easy.

Schedule (days/hours)

Monday thru Friday

Responsibilities

Greeting: Create a warm, welcoming environment and make every patient feel valued from the moment they arrive.
Guiding: Support patients throughout their visit, including check-in/check-out, appointment scheduling, insurance verification and answering questions about their care.
Treatment Support: Help patients understand treatment recommendations, payment options and available financial arrangements.
Patient Experience: Build trusting relationships with patients and help make their dental experience comfortable and stress-free.
Communication: Answer phones, respond to patient questions and communicate clearly with patients, doctors and the dental team.
Scheduling: Maintain an efficient schedule and help maximize opportunities for patients to receive the care they need.
Gratitude: Show genuine appreciation for every patient and create an experience that makes them feel cared for and confident in choosing us.

Qualifications

1+ year of experience in a dental, healthcare, medical, hospitality or customer-service environment preferred.
Knowledge of dental terminology preferred.
Strong communication and interpersonal skills.
A genuine passion for helping people.
Ability to build rapport and create positive relationships with patients.
Strong organization and attention to detail.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.
A positive, professional and patient-first approach.

Why You’ll Love This Role

This isn’t just a front-office position. You’ll play an important role in helping patients feel comfortable, understand their care and take the next step toward a healthier smile.

You’ll have the opportunity to build relationships with patients, work alongside a supportive dental team and develop valuable skills in healthcare, customer experience and dental practice operations.

Preferred Qualifications

Previous experience in a dental or medical office setting

$25-$27

jobs.title: Clinical Case Manager
jobs.description:
Job Overview

Duties and Responsibilities

Ensures supervision of all home care personnel, as assigned:
Enforces/ demonstrates compliance with State/ Federal regulations.
Ensures effective communication to coordinate the implementation of each patient’s Plan of Care.
Instruct, train, and re-educate on clinical skills/procedures when necessary.
Responsible for direct supervision of field LVNs/LPNs/RNs per State guidelines.
Provides support, guidance, and education to patients/patient families and or caregivers to maintain optimal physical and emotional wellbeing.
Communicates all occurrences and other pertinent information to the Clinical Supervisor/Director of Clinical Services.
Ensures any observed or suspected child/adult abuse, neglect, or exploitation is reported to proper authorities as mandated as a health professional.
Collaborates with Clinical Supervisor and Director of Clinical Services to resolve client/clinical concerns in a timely manner.

Company Description

Join an Award-Winning Personal Injury Law Firm

At The Ward Law Group, Our Mission Is Simple

Changing Lives. One Client at a Time

Recognized as one of the Best Places to Work for consecutive years, we are committed to delivering exceptional legal representation while creating an environment where talented professionals can grow, lead, and make a meaningful impact every day.

We believe our people are our greatest asset. We foster a collaborative, innovative, and high-accountability culture where every team member is empowered to make informed decisions, continuously improve, and deliver exceptional results for our clients. Every role contributes directly to helping injured individuals navigate one of the most challenging times in their lives while supporting the continued growth and success of our firm.

Our Core Values

Faith
– We act with integrity, honesty, and purpose in everything we do.

Accountability
– We take ownership of our work, our commitments, and the results we deliver.

Leadership
– We lead by example, inspire others, embrace continuous improvement, and develop high-performing teams.

Loyalty
– We build lasting relationships through trust, respect, and dedication to our clients, teammates, and community.

Service to Our Clients
– We are committed to delivering compassionate, responsive, and exceptional service that maximizes every client's opportunity for success.

Service to Our Teammates
– We foster a culture of collaboration, respect, support, and shared success where every team member has the opportunity to grow and thrive.

Service to Our Community
– We believe in making a positive impact beyond the workplace by serving and strengthening the communities where we live and work.

If you are passionate about helping injured clients, thrive in a fast-paced, results-driven environment, and are committed to delivering exceptional client service while continuously growing your career, we invite you to join The Ward Law Group and help us change lives—one client at a time.

Job Description

The Ward Law Group is seeking an experienced Senior Case Manager to join our New York personal injury team.

This is an opportunity for an accomplished personal injury professional who can independently manage a high-volume caseload while providing exceptional service to clients throughout the life of their cases.

The ideal candidate has extensive New York personal injury experience, strong knowledge of New York procedures and deadlines, and experience handling cases involving auto accidents, premises liability, construction/Labor Law matters, and other complex personal injury claims.

As a senior member of the team, you will also serve as a resource and mentor to junior case managers and support staff.

Key Responsibilities

Manage approximately 75–150+ personal injury cases from intake through settlement or litigation transition
Maintain regular communication with clients regarding case status, treatment, documentation, and next steps
Gather, organize, and review medical records, medical bills, accident reports, insurance information, and supporting documentation
Follow up with medical providers to ensure records and bills are obtained timely
Monitor statutes of limitations, CPLR deadlines, No-Fault requirements, and other critical New York case deadlines
Prepare correspondence, demand packages, case summaries, and documentation supporting settlement negotiations
Assist attorneys with discovery, bills of particulars, depositions, IMEs, and litigation preparation
Coordinate with insurance carriers, medical providers, opposing counsel, and other parties
Assist with NYSCEF filings and case documentation
Identify and track Medicare, Medicaid, health insurance, workers' compensation, and other potential liens
Support settlement and disbursement processes to ensure files are resolved accurately and efficiently
Maintain accurate and detailed case notes within the firm's case management system
Mentor and support junior case managers, paralegals, and other team members
Maintain strong productivity, quality, and client-service standards in a high-volume environment

Client Communication

Contact clients within 24 hours of receiving their case to introduce themselves.
Present initial settlement offers to clients within 48 hours of receipt.
Educate clients about further medical treatments such as injections, rhizotomies, surgeries, TBI treatment, etc.
Inform clients about the necessity to file lawsuits.
Return all client calls the same day.
Maintain bi-weekly communication with clients to ensure effective communication.
Inform clients of case settlements and explain the reductions process.

Insurance Communication

Follow up with insurance companies within 10 days after a settlement demand is sent and continue timely follow-ups until a response is received.
Communicate settlement offers and counteroffers under the direct supervision of an attorney.
Conduct settlement negotiations under the direct supervision of an attorney.
Confirm coverage information (UM, PIP, and BI coverages).
Follow up on Declaration pages from PIP, BI, UM, and UM Rejection forms if applicable.
Send UM subrogation waivers and follow up to confirm UM subrogation is waived.
Schedule mediations.
Prepare mediation/global settlement/settlement conference summaries or presentations.

File Notation

Log initial offers within 24 hours of receipt.
Maintain thorough and accurate notes/records in Litify.
Keep client files updated in Litify.
Track offers, demands, and client authority in the negotiation link.
Save documents or photos in the appropriate folder.
Enter case resolution details in the resolution link.
Pay outstanding invoices and keep the expenses link updated.
Review and update links for injuries and treatment, approval requests, liens, Litify notes, litigations, negotiations, requests, resolutions, etc.
Use appropriate call subjects when logging calls.

Case Review

Review settlement offers before sending them to insurance companies.
Revise surgical case reviews before clients undergo procedures.
Conduct weekly audits for all cases.
Discharge cases as needed.
Draft and file lawsuits on behalf of the attorney, when applicable.
Dismiss lawsuits on behalf of the attorney, when applicable.

Provider Communication

Obtain estimates from providers before closing cases.
Follow up and obtain health insurance liens.
Check provider balances and obtain POD leader authority before settling cases with hospitals.

Client Service

Ensure high standards of client service and satisfaction.
Address client concerns and inquiries promptly and professionally.
Contact clients every 14 days.
Return client voicemails the same day.

Qualifications

Bilingual in English and Spanish required
4–7+ years of personal injury case management experience
Strong New York personal injury experience required
Experience managing approximately 75–150+ active cases
Experience handling cases from intake through settlement and/or litigation
Experience with auto accident cases required; experience with premises liability, construction/Labor Law, and medical malpractice matters strongly preferred
Prior leadership, supervisory, training, or mentoring experience preferred
Strong understanding of New York CPLR deadlines and statutes of limitations
Knowledge of New York No-Fault/Article 51 and serious injury threshold requirements
Knowledge of municipal notice-of-claim requirements involving entities such as NYC or the MTA is a plus
Familiarity with discovery, bills of particulars, depositions, IMEs, and NYSCEF
Understanding of Medicare, Medicaid, private health insurance, and workers' compensation liens
Strong written and verbal communication skills
Excellent organization, deadline management, and attention to detail
Ability to work effectively with injured clients while maintaining professionalism, empathy, and urgency

Education

Bachelor's degree preferred; or
Paralegal certificate or associate's degree

Applicants must be authorized to work in the United States. The Ward Law Group does not provide employment visa sponsorship now or in the future for this position.

Experience with personal injury or legal case management platforms such as:

Litify
SmartAdvocate
Filevine
CASEpeer
Clio
Similar legal case management platforms

Proficiency with Microsoft Office, document management systems, and electronic filing tools is also expected.

What Success Looks Like

A successful Senior Case Manager at The Ward Law Group is highly organized, proactive, and accountable. You understand that strong case management means more than maintaining a file — it means moving cases forward, anticipating deadlines and obstacles, keeping clients informed, and partnering with attorneys to achieve the best possible outcome.

Other Duties

Please note this job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive listing of activities or responsibilities that are required of the employee for this job. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice.

Work Location

This position is based in our New York City office located at 535 5th Avenue, Suite 2600, New York, NY 10017.

Professional development and continuing education support
Collaborative, growth-oriented team environment

If you're looking for an opportunity to grow your litigation career, maximize client recoveries, and work alongside a high-performing legal team, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and become part of a team committed to excellence, accountability, and changing lives—one client at a time.

May assess research subjects' eligibility for inclusion in a particular protocol based on contracts with physicians and nurses and knowledge of the protocol. (essential)
Checks all eligibility and ineligibility criteria with the research subjects' medical record. Verifies information with clinical research nurse and/or principal investigator. (essential)
Discusses informed consent with research subjects. Interacts with research subjects prior to entering the study and throughout the entire treatment. Assists with scheduling appointments and follow up tests. (essential)
Learns protocol and monitors strict adherence to protocols by physicians, nurses and research subjects. Reviews protocol requirements with physicians, nurses and fellows. Identifies any problems with protocol compliance and notifies principal investigator and/or research nurse. Begins to learn how to independently resolve problems with protocol. (essential)
Extracts data on protocol subjects from hospital records, outpatient charts and private physician office records in order to complete case report forms required by specific protocols. Enters data into computerized system. (essential)
Assists clinic staff in obtaining insurance approval for subject protocol participation and scheduling tests and arranging admissions or outpatient visits for subjects. (essential)
Assists investigator with correspondence with IRB. (essential)
As needed, may function in areas/clinics performing job duties related to clinical research studies.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree required.
1-2 years of related work experience required.
Medical terminology.
Working knowledge of computer systems required, including web-based applications and some Microsoft Office applications, which may include Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint or Access.

Competencies

Decision Making:
Ability to make decisions that are based on specific instructions, standard practices and established procedures which generally require little or no supervision.

Problem Solving:
Ability to address problems that are routine, somewhat repetitive and generally solved by following clear directions and procedures and by identifying opportunities for process improvements.

Independence of Action:
Ability to follow general instructions and procedures as provided. Work is monitored by supervisor/manager.

Written Communications:
Ability to communicate clearly and effectively in written English with internal and external customers.

Oral Communications:
Ability to comprehend and converse in English to communicate effectively with medical center staff, patients, families and external customers.

Knowledge:
Ability to demonstrate full working knowledge of standard concepts, practices, procedures and policies with the ability to use them in varied situations.

Teamwork:
Ability to work collaboratively in small teams to improve the operations of immediate work group by offering ideas, identifying issues, and respecting team members.

Customer Service:
Ability to provide a high level of customer service to patients, visitors, staff and external customers in a professional, service-oriented, respectful manner using skills in active listening and problem solving. Ability to remain calm in stressful situations.

Physical Requirements

Light work: Exerting up to 20 pounds of force frequently to move objects. Some elements of the job are sedentary, but the employee will be required to stand for periods of time or move throughout the hospital campus.

Exceptional support from leadership and teammates.

A workplace where you’re valued, your voice is heard, and your work truly matters.

jobs.description:
Company Description

At Lucile Packard Children’s Hospital Stanford, we know world-renowned care begins with world-class caring. That's why we combine advanced technologies and breakthrough discoveries with family-centered care. It's why we provide our caregivers with continuing education and state-of-the-art facilities, like the newly remodeled Lucile Packard Children's Hospital Stanford. And it's why we need caring, committed people on our team - like you. Join us on our mission to heal humanity, one child and family at a time.

Job ID:
P140091-2660347

Job Description

JOB SUMMARY

This paragraph summarizes the general nature, level and purpose of the job.

Case Managers are licensed nursing professionals responsible for coordinating continuum of care and discharge planning activities for a caseload of assigned patients. Major responsibilities include coordinating all facets of a patient's admission/discharge; performing utilization review activities, including review of patient charts for timeliness of services as well as appropriate utilization of services; and ensuring optimum use of resources, service delivery, and compliance with external review agencies' requirements. Case Managers act as consultants to the clinical team, service lines, and other departments regarding patient assessment and patient care and participate in program development and quality improvement initiatives. In their role, Case Managers, by applying guidelines and collaborating with multidisciplinary teams, influence and direct the delivery and quality of patient care. A hospital-based case management system has as its primary goal to ensure the most appropriate use of services by patients and, toward that end, to avoid duplication and misuse of medical services, control costs by reducing inefficient services, and improve the effectiveness of care delivery. Objectives are to facilitate timely discharge; prompt, efficient use of resources; achievement of expected outcomes; collaborative practice; coordination of care across the continuum; and performance/quality improvement activities that lead to optimal patient outcomes. A Case Manager differs from other roles in professional nursing/health care practice in that it is not intended to provide direct patient care; rather, a Case Manager will be assigned to specific patients to ensure that the medical services and treatments required are accomplished in the most financially and clinically efficient manner.

Essential Functions

The essential functions listed are typical examples of work performed by positions in this job classification. They are not designed to contain or be interpreted as a comprehensive inventory of all duties, tasks, and responsibilities. Employees may also perform other duties as assigned.

Employees must abide by all Joint Commission Requirements including but not limited to sensitivity to cultural diversity, patient care, patient rights and ethical treatment, safety and security of physical environments, emergency management, teamwork, respect for others, participation in ongoing education and training, communication and adherence to safety and quality programs, sustaining compliance with National Patient Safety Goals, and licensure and health screenings.

Must perform all duties and responsibilities in accordance with the hospital's policies and procedures, including its Service Standards and its Code of Conduct.

COORDINATION OF CARE

Manages each patient's transition through the system and transfers accountability to the appropriate person upon entry into another clinical service or discharge.

DISCHARGE PLANNING

Coordinates and facilitates timely implementation of discharge plans for assigned patients with complex needs in collaboration with other interdisciplinary team members; arranges follow-up care as appropriate.

EDUCATION/CONSULTATION

Acts as an educational resource and provides consultation to patients and their families, hospital medical personnel regarding the discharge planning process and applicable regulatory requirements; educates the staff on case management; and provides specific information related to case types.

LEAD WORK

May lead the work of administrative/clinical support staff responsible for assisting with case management for an assigned patient caseload.

Other

Participates in department program planning, goal setting, systems development and process improvement; participates in department and hospital committees and task forces; develops and maintains documentation of findings, discharge arrangements, and actions taken according to departmental guidelines; prepares and maintains records as required; collects, analyzes and reports on data for utilization, quality improvement, compliance, and other areas as assigned.

PATIENT ASSESSMENT/PLAN OF CARE

Functions as a resource to and collaborates with physicians, social workers, nurses, and other interdisciplinary team members to assess, plan, and coordinate patient care needs and/or performs patient assessment and develops a plan of care to assure consistent, timely, and appropriate care is provided in a patient-focused manner.

QUALITY IMPROVEMENT

Participates in quality improvement activities by identifying opportunities for improvement in such areas as clinical outcomes, utilization of resources and concurrent data collection; participates in clinical process improvement teams within the department, service lines, and hospital.

THIRD-PARTY REIMBURSEMENT

Collects, analyzes, reports and reviews patient information with third-party payors to assure reimbursement for patient services/procedures. Communicates with review organizations/payers to provide requested clinical and psychosocial information to assure reimbursement.

UTILIZATION REVIEW

Reviews prospectively, concurrently and retrospectively all inpatients for appropriateness of admission, level of care, and determines appropriate length of stay. Monitors patients' length of stay and collaborates with physicians to ensure resource utilization remains within covered benefits and are appropriate in relationship to the patient's clinical and psychosocial needs; plans and implements (through multi-disciplinary meetings or rounds) strategies to reduce length of stay, reduce resource consumption, and achieve positive patient outcomes analyzes and addresses aggregate variances as well as variances from individual patients and shares this information with staff, physicians, and administration.

KNOWLEDGE

Ability to resolve conflicts and/or negotiate with others to achieve positive results; establish and maintain effective interpersonal relationships.
Ability to understand, interpret and apply complex federal and state hospital compliance laws, rules, regulations and guidelines.
Ability to work effectively with individuals at all levels of the organization.

Brief Job Description

Under the supervision of the Program Supervisor IV, provides advanced and comprehensive case management consultation for families with children who have health risks, conditions, or special health care needs. Oversees case management services for families in the Children with Special Health Care Needs (CSHCN), Community First Choice (CFC), Newborn Screening (NBS), Personal Care Services (PCS), and Case Management for Children and Pregnant Women programs. Travels to conduct home visits, completes intakes, Family Needs Assessments, Service Plans, and Follow-up Services to families on caseload and to determine eligibility and need for PCS/CFC. Links families to community resources. Conducts presentations and communicates program services and/or changes in a positive and accurate manner. Works as a team member. Actively participates and advocates in Community Resource Coordination Groups (CRCG), case management coalitions, and community organizations. Provides information and referral services. Completes administrative duties, monthly reports, special assignments and work activities in a professional and timely manner. Works collaboratively with public health staff in the event of a regional or state disaster. Works under minimum supervision with considerable latitude for the use of initiative and independent judgment. Will have immunizations current that are necessary to maintain immunity or show immunity to specific diseases. Staff required on an as-needed basis to assist with a response and/or recovery effort because of their subject matter expertise and/or experience.

Essential Job Functions (EJFs)

Attends work on a regular and predictable schedule in accordance with agency leave policy and performs other duties as assigned.

(45%) Case Management Functions—Provides complex and specialized social work consultation and comprehensive case management services to families who receive services or are seeking services from the CSHCN, SSI, NBS, PCS, CFC and Case Management for Children and Pregnant Women programs. Conducts home visits for comprehensive assessment of home environment and needs. Following program guidelines, provides comprehensive case management services including the Intake, Family Needs Assessment, Service Plan, and Follow-up services. Assists families with the eligibility determination process for CSHCN. Provides information and referral services, linkage to community resources, family supports, advocacy, and service coordination. Maintains documentation of work activities, monthly reports, travel reports, case summaries and correspondence. Utilizes software programs to do database entry, word processing, spreadsheets, electronic mail, and Internet.

Conducts comprehensive assessments to determine eligibility and need for PCS. Conducts assessments during home visits with families. Documents identified needs and forwards documentation for authorization of personal care services. Conducts reassessments for PCS as required or as necessary according to family needs. Enters family encounter information into an online database.

(20%) Technical Assistance/Quality Assurance/Trainings – Provides consultation, presentations, and training to agencies for programs such as CSHCN, CFC, PCS, Case Management for Children and Pregnant Women and Family Support Services. Assists in training new staff, volunteers and social work interns. Provides program presentations to public to promote awareness of services available to children with health risks, conditions or special health care needs. Participates as a team member with peer chart reviews for regional internal quality assurance.

(20%) Community Organization/Resource Development -- Actively participates in community organization functions and collaborates with other community entities on health, social work, case management and other related issues. Serves as the representative for the Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS) on the CRCG, coalitions, interagency groups and advocacy groups to collaborate efforts in serving children with special health care needs. Maintains social service directory of community resources for service area.

(15%) Professional & Team Development -- Attends trainings and conferences relevant to job to meet licensing requirement and provides backup and support to other team members. Continues to develop professional knowledge and skill in the practice of Social Work/Case Management in the Public Health setting. Participates in performance evaluations process. Attends staff meetings. Performs other duties as assigned. In the event of a regional or statewide disaster, all staff will participate, assist, and support all regional and/or state wide disaster relief efforts. Responds to and supports regional/statewide disaster relief efforts.

Children’s programs, such as Medicaid, CSHCN, CPW, SSI, NBS, Lead, Early Childhood Intervention (ECI).

jobs.title: Care Coordinator - Rehab
jobs.description:
Help Patients Heal. Make a Difference Every Day.

At Complete Care, we're committed to helping injured patients recover through compassionate care, seamless experiences, and exceptional clinical support. Every role on our team contributes to creating a healing environment where patients receive the care, attention, and encouragement they deserve.

As a Care Coordinator (Rehab), you'll play an essential role in each patient's recovery by delivering provider-directed therapies, helping patients feel comfortable throughout their treatment, and ensuring every step of their care is completed with accuracy, efficiency, and compassion.

This is an excellent opportunity for someone beginning or growing a career in healthcare who enjoys helping people, values organization, embraces continuous learning, and takes pride in delivering high-quality patient care.

If you're dependable, kind, detail-oriented, and thrive in a collaborative clinical environment where patients always come first, we'd love to meet you.

What You'll Do

Deliver provider-directed rehabilitation therapies safely and accurately.
Prepare patients for therapy and explain what to expect.
Help patients stay on track with their prescribed treatment plans.
Document therapies accurately in the electronic medical record (EHR).
Educate patients on therapy exercises and the proper use of Durable Medical Equipment (DME).
Monitor patient progress and communicate concerns to providers when appropriate.
Verify insurance information and support authorization workflows.
Coordinate closely with providers and teammates to deliver a seamless patient experience.
Maintain an organized treatment area while supporting efficient daily clinic operations.
Deliver every patient interaction with professionalism, empathy, and a commitment to excellence.
Look for opportunities to improve processes, support your team, and enhance the patient experience.

You'll Thrive Here If You Are...

Calm—You stay composed and reassuring, even during busy clinic days.
Reliable—Your team knows they can count on you to follow through on your commitments.
Organized—You naturally keep things in order and don't let details fall through the cracks.
Accurate—You understand that every detail matters because every patient matters.
Process-Driven—You enjoy following established procedures while continuously looking for better ways to improve efficiency and patient care.
Warm & Personable—You enjoy building relationships and helping patients feel comfortable and confident throughout their recovery.
A Strong Multitasker—You can balance patient care, documentation, and communication without sacrificing quality or urgency.
Compassionate—Helping others motivates you every day.
Team-Oriented—You believe the best patient outcomes come from working together and supporting one another.
Professional—You take ownership of your work and hold yourself to high standards of quality, accountability, and service.

Preferred Experience

Physical Therapy Aide
Rehabilitation Technician
Chiropractic Assistant
Patient Care
Customer Service
Healthcare

No healthcare experience? That's okay.

We provide comprehensive training for dependable, patient-focused individuals who demonstrate professionalism, strong communication skills, adaptability, and a genuine desire to learn and grow.

What Success Looks Like

Patients feel welcomed, informed, and supported throughout every stage of their recovery.
Therapies are delivered safely, accurately, and consistently.
Documentation is complete, timely, and supports exceptional continuity of care.
Care plans stay on track, allowing patients to recover as efficiently as possible.
Providers and teammates rely on your communication, organization, and follow-through.
You actively contribute ideas that improve workflows, strengthen teamwork, and enhance the patient experience.
You help create a positive, collaborative clinic culture where excellence is the standard.

If you enjoy bringing order to busy days, helping people heal, embracing new ways to improve care, and taking pride in meaningful work that changes lives, you'll fit right in.

Why Complete Care?

We're a growing multidisciplinary healthcare organization committed to delivering exceptional injury care while creating rewarding careers for compassionate, high-performing team members.

We invest in advanced technology, ongoing training, coaching, and career development because we believe empowered employees create exceptional patient experiences. By fostering collaboration, innovation, and continuous improvement, we're building the future of injury recovery—one patient, one teammate, and one success story at a time.

If you're looking for a place where your work has purpose, your ideas are valued, your growth is supported, and every day gives you the opportunity to make a meaningful impact, Complete Care is the place to grow your career.

Benefits

Competitive Salary
Medical, Dental & Vision Insurance
401(k) with Company Match
Paid Time Off
Paid Sick Leave
Paid Holidays + Floating Holiday
Company-Paid Life Insurance

GEO provides complementary, turnkey solutions for numerous government partners worldwide across a spectrum of diversified correctional and community reentry services. From the development of state-of-the-art facilities and the provision of management services and evidence-based rehabilitation to the post-release reintegration and supervision of individuals in the community, GEO offers fully diversified, cost-effective services that deliver enhanced quality and improved outcomes.

The Case Manager provides counseling services, assists the inmates or detainees in adjusting to facility life and obtaining needed services or changes in assignment. Harmony School of Excellence - Houston (K-8)

JOB GOAL
:Provide administrative and clerical support to campus and district special education and Section 504 staff to facilitate the timely and efficient completion of administrative responsibilities associated with the ARD/IEP and Section 504 processes, student records, data management, and Special Programs operations. The SPED Case Manager Assistant supports case managers, special education teachers, ARD facilitators/coordinators, Section 504 coordinators, evaluation personnel, and other designated staff by coordinating meetings, preparing and distributing required notices and documents, maintaining records, tracking timelines and documentation, entering designated data, and performing other administrative functions. Responsibilities requiring professional judgment or committee decision-making remain with appropriately qualified professional staff and the applicable ARD or Section 504 committee.

Position Qualifications

High School Diploma or GED
Minimum 2 years of clerical experience (preferred)
Experience supporting special education, Section 504, student records, or other compliance-related educational

processes (preferred)

Experience with student information systems, special education management systems, or other education-related

software (preferred)

Duties And Responsibilities

Understands and supports the mission, vision and values of Harmony Public Schools.
Coordinates and schedules ARD committee meetings in collaboration with case managers, evaluation personnel, and

other appropriate staff.

Assists with ARD meeting logistics, including calendar invitations, participant coordination, room reservations, and other

scheduling arrangements.

Prepares and distributes ARD meeting notices and other required administrative notifications in accordance with

established district procedures.

Contacts parents/guardians regarding ARD meeting scheduling, confirmations, rescheduling, and other routine

administrative matters related to the ARD process.

Provides or distributes Procedural Safeguards and other required notices and documents to parents/guardians and

maintains documentation of distribution as required.

Distributes finalized IEP/ARD documents and other required documents to parents/guardians following ARD meetings in

accordance with district procedures.

Prepares and distributes teacher information packets/bundles and relevant student documents to appropriate staff at the

beginning of the school year and following ARD meetings, as directed.

Tracks ARD schedules, administrative deadlines, required documents, signatures, consents, and other assigned timelines

and provides reminders or follow-up to appropriate staff.

Follows up with designated staff regarding ARD records that have not been finalized, submitted, or archived within

established timelines.

Assists case managers, diagnosticians, LSSPs, SLPs, and other appropriate staff with administrative tasks associated

with the ARD/IEP process.

Coordinates and schedules initial, annual, reevaluation, and other Section 504 meetings in collaboration with case

manager and other designated staff.

Assists with Section 504 meeting logistics, including calendar invitations, participant coordination, room reservations, and

other scheduling arrangements.

Prepares and distributes Section 504 meeting notices, parent notices, and other required administrative documents in

accordance with established district procedures.

Contacts parents/guardians regarding Section 504 meeting scheduling, confirmations, rescheduling, and other routine

administrative matters.

Distributes finalized Section 504 Plans and other required documents to parents/guardians and appropriate staff in

accordance with district procedures.

Assists with distributing Section 504 accommodation information to teachers and other appropriate staff at the beginning

of the school year, following Section 504 meetings, and when appropriate due to student schedule or placement changes.

Tracks Section 504 meeting schedules, reevaluation dates, required documentation, parent responses, and other

Scans, uploads, files, archives, and retrieves Section 504 records and supporting documentation in the district's

records requests when students transfer.

Follows up with designated staff regarding missing Section 504 documentation, records that have not been finalized or

archived, upcoming meetings, and other administrative items requiring completion.

Maintains accurate, organized, and confidential electronic and physical special education and Section 504 records in

accordance with district procedures and applicable records-retention requirements.

Scans, uploads, files, archives, retrieves, and organizes ARD/IEP documents, Section 504 documents, evaluations,

consent forms, protocols, and other student records.

Description

The Case Manager III provides supportive case management and care coordination services to individuals. Working under the guidance of the Program Manager and alongside an interdisciplinary team, the Case Manager III helps patients access behavioral health, substance use disorder (SUD), medical, and community-based services.

This is an excellent opportunity for candidates who are early in their behavioral health careers and are interested in developing skills in case management, care coordination, substance use treatment, and patient engagement. The position utilizes evidence-based approaches including Motivational Interviewing, Strengths-Based Case Management, and ASAM-informed care.

The Case Manager III is expected to demonstrate empathy, professionalism, strong organizational skills, cultural humility, and a commitment to supporting patients on their recovery journey.

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

Clinical Services & Patient Support

Assist with patient intake, screenings, and basic needs assessments.
Support the completion of ASAM-informed screening and referral processes under clinical supervision, as appropriate.
Help patients identify goals related to their health, recovery, and overall well-being.
Utilize Motivational Interviewing and strengths-based approaches to engage and support patients.
Coordinate referrals to behavioral health, substance use treatment, medical providers, housing resources, and community services.
Conduct outreach and follow-up to ensure patients successfully connect with recommended services.
Provide warm handoffs and assist with closed-loop referral processes.
Support patients during challenging situations and notify supervisors of crisis concerns according to program protocols.
Maintain accurate and timely documentation in electronic health records and other required systems.
Communicate patient progress and care coordination activities with team members.

Care Coordination & Team Collaboration

Participate in multidisciplinary team meetings and case review discussions.
Collaborate with internal programs including Admissions, Residential Services, Outpatient Services, Opioid Treatment Program (OTP), Perinatal Services, and other programs as needed.
Work collaboratively with community partners, healthcare providers, probation departments, and social service agencies.
Assist in outreach and engagement efforts for patients referred by internal and external partners.
Support integrated care efforts across substance use, behavioral health, and primary care services.

Administrative Responsibilities

Complete required documentation, reports, and data tracking activities.
Attend required trainings, team meetings, and supervision sessions.
Maintain compliance with HIPAA, 42 CFR Part 2, and organizational policies.

new_jobs.title: Principal Technical Program Manager
new_jobs.description:
Our Mission

You call. You wait. You call again. In every other part of your life, you book in seconds. In healthcare, you’re blocked.

We’re here to give power to the patient.

For nearly 20 years, we’ve built the leading healthcare marketplace - helping tens of millions of people find and book the care they need. Now, we’re going further: building our infrastructure beyond Zocdoc’s marketplace to power access to care wherever patients search, from provider websites and insurance directories to search engines, AI platforms, and more.

Healthcare still lacks something every other major consumer industry takes for granted: a seamless way to go from seeking to getting . We don’t want to own the front door to care; there isn't one. We want to make sure all of those doors open when patients are knocking.

Fixing healthcare starts with fixing access to it. And we're still just getting started.

Your Impact to the Mission

Zocdoc's most important asset is our people. As a Principal Technical Program Manager for Practice Solutions, you will own and drive the most complex, cross-functional technical programs across the business unit, the initiatives that span multiple engineering teams and product domains and that no single team can deliver alone. Practice Solutions powers how healthcare practices run their day to day across every patient access channel: phone, web, marketplace, and partner syndication. That includes Zo, our AI phone assistant, along with our provider directory and booking platform, intake and pre-appointment workflows, calendar and scheduling experiences, and the services that keep availability accurate across channels. You'll operate at the intersection of Engineering, Product, Design, Analytics, and go-to-market leadership to deliver scalable, highly available, multi-tenant SaaS capabilities. You'll bring structure to ambiguity, drive sequencing across teams, surface architectural and operational risk early, and keep the trains running on time, all while raising the bar for how program execution happens across the entire business unit. This is a highly visible role with significant autonomy and influence.

You'll enjoy this role if you are…

Inspired by the opportunity to positively impact the healthcare experience for millions of patients and providers
A platform thinker who instinctively looks beyond individual features to understand how systems connect, scale, and evolve over time
Energized by building structure in ambiguous, high-complexity environments where multiple teams, products, and priorities intersect
Comfortable operating at both 30,000 feet and in the architectural details, able to reason about distributed systems, reliability tradeoffs, and multi-tenant SaaS constraints
Unafraid to drive movement and accountability at every level of the organization, regardless of title or tenure
Calm and decisive in high-stakes situations, especially when sequencing work across teams with shared platform dependencies
A strong influencer who can align engineering leaders, product leaders, and cross-functional stakeholders around shared outcomes even when ownership boundaries are unclear
A believer that diverse and inclusive teams and cultures are non-negotiable

Your day to day is…

Organizing and driving the business unit's planning cadence, coordinating inputs and stakeholders across engineering and product and keeping the cycle on track so strategy turns into a clear, committed, sequenced roadmap
Leading large, multi-quarter platform initiatives that span the Practice Solutions product scope, keeping each part on schedule and the whole program moving
Translating high-level business and product goals into structured program plans with clear sequencing, milestones, dependencies, and measurable outcomes
Building the reporting and transparency that give leadership a clear, honest view of status, dependencies, and risk
Partnering closely with senior engineering leaders to anticipate architectural and operational risks before they surface in production
Digging into technical issues at the seams between teams, triaging, framing the problem clearly, and pulling the right architects and engineers together to solve it
Surfacing tradeoffs between speed, scope, reliability, and technical debt, and facilitating clear, well-reasoned decisions at the right level
Clarifying ownership boundaries and reducing cross-team friction where systems, incentives, or customer journeys overlap
Establishing and refining lightweight mechanisms that improve transparency, accountability, and long-term platform health
Communicating program status, risks, and key decisions clearly to executive stakeholders and business unit leadership

You'll be successful in this role if you have…

A strong bias to action and an ownership mentality
8+ years in Technical Program Management, Engineering Program Management, or a similar technical leadership role
A track record delivering large-scale, cross-functional initiatives in a product-led SaaS environment
A strong understanding of distributed systems, cloud architectures (AWS or equivalent), and event-driven systems
Demonstrated ability to reason about architectural tradeoffs without owning implementation, and enough technical depth to hold your own in a room full of senior engineers
Experience driving programs that span multiple engineering teams with shared platform dependencies
The confidence to drive accountability and momentum across all levels of an organization without relying on formal authority
Excellent communication skills, including clear written status and risk framing for both engineers and executives
A Bachelor's degree in a technical field (e.g., Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems) or equivalent practical experience
Experience in healthcare or another regulated, multi-tenant domain is a plus
Humility. You believe in treating all people with dignity and respect, regardless of title or tenure, and you approach tough conversations with empathy

Benefits

Flexible, hybrid work environment at our convenient Soho location
Unlimited Vacation
100% paid employee health benefit options (including medical, dental, and vision)
Commuter Benefits
401(k) with employer funded match
Corporate wellness program with Wellhub
Sabbatical leave (for employees with 5+ years of service)
Competitive paid parental leave and fertility/family planning reimbursement
Cell phone reimbursement
Catered lunch everyday along with beverages and snacks
Employee Resource Groups and ZocClubs to promote shared community and belonging

Zocdoc is committed to fair and equitable compensation practices. Salary ranges are determined through alignment with market data. Base salary offered is determined by a number of factors including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and skills. Certain positions are also eligible for variable pay and/or equity; your recruiter will discuss the full compensation package details.

NYC Base Salary Range

$195,000—$250,000 USD

About Us

Zocdoc is the country’s leading digital health marketplace that helps patients easily find and book the care they need. Each month, millions of patients use our free service to find nearby, in-network providers, compare choices based on verified patient reviews, and instantly book in-person or video visits online. Providers participate in Zocdoc’s Marketplace to reach new patients to grow their practice, fill their last-minute openings, and deliver a better healthcare experience. Founded in 2007 with a mission to give power to the patient, our work each day in pursuit of that mission is guided by our six core values. Zocdoc is a private company backed by some of the world’s leading investors, and we believe we’re still only scratching the surface of what we plan to accomplish.

Zocdoc is a mission-driven organization dedicated to building teams as diverse as the patients and providers we aim to serve. In the spirit of one of our core values - Together, Not Alone , we are a company that prides itself on being highly collaborative, and we believe that diverse perspectives, experiences and contributors make our community and our platform better. We’re an equal opportunity employer committed to providing employees with a work environment free of discrimination and harassment. Applicants are considered for employment regardless of race, color, ethnicity, ancestry, religion, national origin, gender, sex, gender identity, gender expression, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital or parental status, disability, veteran status, or any other class protected by applicable laws.

Community Health Worker

new_jobs.description:
